subject: Fallback engagement window - RTO alignment and regional activation variance
messages:
From: Amit Chopra <amit.chopra@orchid-payments.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: SRE Team <sre@orchid-payments.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial: Fallback engagement window and RTO concern for US+EU

Hi Sean,

Quick note from our compliance and SRE side: we reviewed the proposed Redwood standby activation timeline and it looks like the default regional fallback window (up to 4 hours to achieve full traffic cutover + DNS propagation) will put us outside the 2-hour RTO required for a subset of our regulatory accounts in the EU.

We understand architecture constraints, but we need to explore whether Redwood can offer a narrower engagement window for our EU traffic (or a contractual exception paired with compensating controls).

Key asks:
- Can Redwood commit to a 2-hour RTO for EU region failover for payments traffic?
- If not, what options do we have (pre-warm warm-standby, reserved pool for quick activation, regional read-only replicas to shorten RPO)?
- Any evidence/metrics you can share about typical switchover latency and post-cutover consistency?

We can escalate on our side but wanted to get an action plan together this week.

Thanks,
Amit Chopra
Head of Infrastructure
Orchid Payments

Amit — thanks for the clear write-up. Short answers up front: we can get you closer to a 2-hour RTO, but it will require a mix of engineering changes (pre-warmed standby + tighter replication windows) and a contractual SLA addendum to capture the different activation profile + cost delta.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick sync (30m) today to align on scope (payments-only traffic, specific EU regions). I have Marissa (delivery) and Karthik (solutions) on the thread.
2) Marissa to propose two technical options with estimated lead times and cost impact.
3) We produce an SLA addendum draft that maps RTO/RPO per traffic class and activation path.

If that sounds good I’ll schedule a 11:30 call.

Amit / Sean — following up with concrete options after the call. I summarized the trade-offs below; full numbers attached (replication-latency.csv) and the procedural runbook is attached as a stub PDF.

Option A — Aggressive pre-warm (recommended for payments-only):
- Keep a dedicated warm-standby pool for EU payments (hot replicas + warmed runtime).
- Activation flow: traffic cutover + KV cache sync + DNS TTL 30s => projected median switchover 45–90 minutes; 95th percentile ~110 minutes under current benchmarks.
- Cost: reserved capacity + standby warm hours; estimated +32% TCO for covered traffic.
- Pros: meets 2-hour RTO target consistently in our internal tests.
- Cons: higher reserved-cost footprint; longer procurement lead time to reserve capacity.

Option B — Staged activation with read-replicas (lower cost):
- Use regional read-only replicas to reduce RPO; full runtime instantiation on cutover.
- Activation flow: replica promotion + runtime spin + DNS => projected median 2–3 hours; could miss 2-hour target at 95th percentile.
- Cost: lower ongoing cost, higher complexity on failback.

Option C — Contractual exception + fallbacks (for a subset of regulated accounts):
- Maintain current multi-region fallback (4-hour window) but add compensating controls: active replay window, extended monitoring, and an SLA credit schedule for failures that exceed 2 hours.
- Useful if procurement won’t accept price uplift.

Attachments included:
- runbook-standby-activation.pdf (application/pdf)
- replication-latency.csv (text/csv)

I’ll produce an SLA addendum draft (option A + insertion for scoped accounts) and share pricing. Tagging Karthik for final architecture note.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Delivery
Redwood Inference

Team — thanks, that framing helps. We prefer Option A for the highest-risk merchant segments. A few follow-ups:
- Can you provide the runbook and latency CSV to our auditors? We’ll need them for our internal risk board.
- Rough order-of-magnitude (RoM) for the monthly uplift and any minimum commitment term?
- We will need an SLA addendum that specifically enumerates RTO for the scoped traffic and a credit schedule; please include language for at-scale partial failovers, not just full-region loss.

If you can send the draft addendum today we’ll circulate it internally and aim for a procurement review next week.

—Amit

Date: 2028-07-30T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: Fallback engagement window and RTO concern for US+EU — legal flags and next steps

Looping in a quick legal note before we draft:
- If we surface Option A as a contractual SLA (2-hr RTO for scoped payments traffic) we need to: 1) tightly define "scoped traffic" (specific APIs/endpoints, IP prefixes, and account IDs), 2) carve out force majeure/partial region degradations, and 3) include explicit remediation/credit calculation tied to observed activation time (not subjective reporting).
- Also recommend a pilot period (60 days) where we operate Option A as an operational offering without credits to validate metrics, then convert to an SLA after pilot acceptance. This reduces legal exposure while giving Orchid the stronger guarantee during the pilot through an operational commitment letter.

I’ll draft the SLA addendum language and a pilot MOU — will circulate the docx here (sla-addendum-draft.docx).

—Olga
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
